title: Manicouagan Reservoir – the eye of Quebec

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find something strange in central Quebec.
From orbit it looks like a giant eye, a perfect circle about seventy kilometers across.
The blue ring surrounds a solitary island plateau, a quiet landlocked mountain rising in the middle.
People call it the eye of Quebec, but what could have carved such a massive ring?
The impact happened two hundred fourteen million years ago.
A five kilometer meteor created a crater about one hundred kilometers wide.
Water later filled the inner ring, leaving the island plateau high above the lake.
So that mysterious eye is really a giant impact crater turned lake.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir is a seventy kilometer diameter annular lake formed by a meteor impact two hundred fourteen million years ago. The crater's outer ring spans about one hundred kilometers and encloses Rene-Levasseur Island. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: NASA, Wikimedia Commons. Source: Wikipedia.
